records.text: JAY-Z, in partnership with the NFL, controls who performs at the Super Bowl halftime show and booked Bad Bunny.
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: Actually, I looked into it. The person that controls who gets to perform at the halftime is JAY-Z for some reason. ... JAY-Z in partnership with the NFL. ... but JAY-Z booked him.

verification.notes: NFL records confirm that the NFL, Apple Music, and Roc Nation jointly announced Bad Bunny, with Roc Nation serving as executive producer and strategic entertainment adviser; Jay-Z publicly endorsed the selection. This supports a substantial Roc Nation/Jay-Z role, but not the stronger claim that Jay-Z unilaterally controls the halftime show or personally booked Bad Bunny.

records.text: Nielsen estimated that 128 million people watched the Super Bowl game and that viewership increased to 135 million during halftime.
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: Nielsen estimates that 128 million people watched the Super Bowl game last night, forgetting the halftime performance. ... That number increased to 135 million viewers during the halftime performance. So people got up and were like, I don't want to watch the, you know, I'm not watching the whole Super Bowl match,

verification.notes: Nielsen's finalized national measurement reports a 125.6 million average audience for Super Bowl LX and 128.2 million for halftime; it identifies 137.8 million as a second-quarter peak. Those figures directly contradict the statement's 128 million game average and 135 million halftime audience.

records.text: Turning Point USA prerecorded its All-American Halftime Show a couple of weeks before the live Super Bowl halftime performance.
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: We should be clear it was a prerecord. ... so Bad Bunny was performing live, ... Turning Point USA prerecorded, I think, a couple of weeks ago.

verification.notes: Contemporaneous reporting confirms the program was prerecorded in Atlanta rather than broadcast live. The transcript itself hedges the recording date with 'I think,' and no authoritative source located establishes that it was recorded specifically a couple of weeks earlier.

records.text: Turning Point USA's alternative halftime campaign failed to draw viewers away from the NFL.
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: This means that the, I would say, unnecessary Super Bowl political lines that were drawn ... by Turning Point USA was not successful in terms of drawing people away from the NFL's viewership. Now, in case you missed it, when Bad Bunny was announced,

verification.notes: Nielsen's finalized measurement shows the NFL halftime audience averaged 128.2 million, above the full-game average of 125.6 million, while AP observed roughly 5 million concurrent viewers on TPUSA's YouTube stream. These figures support that the NFL retained an overwhelmingly larger audience, but public aggregate counts cannot prove that no viewers were drawn away or establish the counterfactual audience without the alternative.

They got there and were told with doing a split halftime show, a lot of them actually liked Bad Bunny as a bad buddy. ... they also thought that it was going to be a bigger artist because they were told that they were going to contend with the halftime show and they didn't think that they were going to do that

records.text: A source told us President Trump would watch the All-American Halftime Show and that it would get more views than Bad Bunny's halftime show.
records.speaker: Anonymous Source #6 (Ep hWTdXHGQ8R4)

appearances.snippet: the person who was producing this, some guy named Matt (halftime-show producer; surname unverified) was trying to get them hyped by saying there's a little birdie that told us that Trump (Donald J. Trump) is going to be watching our halftime show. ... he also said to them that this is going to get more views than the Bad Bunny halftime show

verification.notes: Transcript context relays a producer's prediction that Trump would watch and the show would beat Bad Bunny. Current results directly contradict the prediction: Trump publicly reviewed Bad Bunny's official show, and Nielsen measured 128.2 million viewers for it versus roughly 5 million concurrent YouTube viewers for TPUSA's show.
